newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, demand weakens.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, demand weakens.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Tuesday, with buyers keeping to the sidelines amid falls in Malaysia, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,650-60 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at 5-10 rupiah below and above the range.

"There seems to be a big difference in prices depending on which seller you are talking to," one trader said. "Some are selling at the lower end while others are trying to keep prices on the high side to match export values."
Traders said export prices continued to be attractive, but added that European values could decline later in the day in tandem with the falls in Malaysia.
They said comments by Beddu Amang, head of the national logistics agency BULOG, that 1,600 rupiah was an "appropriate" price level for palm olein could dampen sentiment.
"Buyers will run," one trader said. "It seems to be an indication that BULOG would like the price to be 1,600."
"But there has been no sign that BULOG is preparing to intervene in the market," he added.
Amang also said that state plantations would increase their monthly crude palm oil allocation to BULOG to 20,000 tonnes from 10,000 tonnes previously.
He said crude palm oil production was projected to rise to 5.2-5.3 million tonnes this year from 4.5 million in 1996.
The traders also said players were keeping a close watch on the rupiah, which regained some ground lost to the U.S. dollar.
"The exchange rate is playing a big part in determining palm olein prices, and sellers are closely watching currency movements for price direction," one trader said.
